Trump is moving to put the White House in control of which NIH grants get funded, according to a Politico report published Saturday, September 19. He has directed his budget director, Russ Vought, to draft an executive order creating a board that would decide which research the National Institutes of Health pays for.

The NIH is the largest funder of medical research in the country. Its budget runs about $48 billion a year, and Congress is the body that approves that money and says what it is for. That funding is behind a huge share of the research into cancer, sickle cell disease, maternal mortality, HIV, diabetes and heart disease, and it flows to universities, teaching hospitals and medical schools all over the country rather than being spent inside one government building.
